section: Right to Information Act 2005 - structure, exemptions, amendments and issues
subsections: Commencement - assent, enactment and coming into force
Achievements vs misuse - transparency gains, frivolous and vexatious applications
RTI activists' safety - attacks and whistle-blower protection

accepted.s: As of July 2026, the approximate number of RTI appeals and complaints pending across Information Commissions was reported to be
o: Over 40,000
Over 10 lakh
Over 1 lakh
Over 4 lakh
accepted.x: More than 4 lakh RTI appeals and complaints were reported to be pending across Information Commissions as of July 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical figure rather than being distracted by nearby order-of-magnitude options.

accepted.s: Which of the following is identified as a major institutional reason for delays in the disposal of RTI matters?
o: Excessive number of constitutional amendments
Absence of judicial review over RTI orders
Compulsory prior approval of Parliament for every RTI application
Chronic vacancies in the Central and State Information Commissions
accepted.x: Chronic vacancies in the Central Information Commission and State Information Commissions, together with a large backlog of appeals, cause long delays.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional cause directly linked to the stated administrative consequence.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the contemporary status of RTI institutions:
1. A 2025 report of Satark Nagrik Sangathan flagged significant gaps in Information Commissions.
2. The report was issued as the RTI Act approached its twentieth anniversary.
3. The report stated that all Information Commissions had completely eliminated pendency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because significant gaps and pendency remained in the Information Commissions.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute claim that an institutional problem has been completely eliminated.

accepted.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 suggested re-examination of the RTI framework mainly in the context of exempting which of the following categories of information?
o: Only information supplied by private bodies
All information held by local authorities
All records relating to public expenditure and contracts
Confidential service records and draft or exploratory policy discussions
accepted.x: The Economic Survey suggested considering exemptions for confidential service records and draft or exploratory policy discussions, along with a possible ministerial veto.
accepted.tq: Match the policy proposal with the specific categories named in it.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was proposed as a possible feature of the Economic Survey 2025-26's suggested re-examination of the RTI regime?
o: A ministerial veto over disclosure in specified cases
A complete abolition of Section 4 disclosure
Transfer of all Information Commissions to the Supreme Court
A constitutional amendment abolishing the right to know
accepted.x: The proposal included the possibility of a ministerial veto in relation to certain confidential or draft policy information.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the specific proposed institutional safeguard from exaggerated alternatives.

accepted.s: The 2019 amendment to the RTI Act raised concerns about the autonomy of Information Commissions because it empowered the Central Government to determine their
o: tenure and salaries
appointment of all Public Information Officers
jurisdiction over constitutional disputes and writ petitions
annual budget without legislative approval
accepted.x: The 2019 amendment allowed the Central Government to prescribe the tenure and salaries of Information Commissioners, raising autonomy concerns.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who controls the service conditions?’ method to identify the autonomy issue.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Passage of the RTI Bill by the Lok Sabha
B. Passage of the RTI Bill by the Rajya Sabha
C. Presidential assent to the RTI Act
D. Full commencement of the RTI Act
Select the correct sequence.
o: A, B, C, D
B, A, C, D
A, C, B, D
C, A, B, D
accepted.x: The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on 11 May 2005, the Rajya Sabha on 12 May 2005, assent was given on 15 June 2005, and the Act fully came into force on 12 October 2005.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the two parliamentary stages between them.
accepted.sec: Commencement - assent, enactment and coming into force

accepted.s: Which of the following provisions came into force immediately upon enactment of the RTI Act, along with Sections 4(1), 5 and 12?
o: Sections 13, 15, 16 and 24
Sections 1, 2 and 3 only
Sections 7, 8, 9 and 10 only
Sections 18, 19, 20 and 22 only
accepted.x: Sections 13, 15, 16 and 24 were among the provisions that came into force immediately, along with Sections 4(1), 5 and 12.
accepted.tq: Test the exception to the general commencement date by recalling the specified section cluster.
accepted.sec: Commencement - assent, enactment and coming into force

accepted.s: Under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act, which of the following is included within the meaning of ‘information’?
o: Information personally generated by an applicant after filing a request
Only physical records maintained by public authorities
Material in any form, including records, e-mails, opinions, contracts, samples and electronic data
Only final judicial decisions published in the Gazette
accepted.x: Section 2(f) covers material in any form, including records, documents, e-mails, opinions, advice, contracts, samples, models and electronic data.
accepted.tq: Choose the option reflecting the broad statutory wording ‘material in any form’.

accepted.s: Information relating to a private body is accessible under Section 2(f) when it is
o: published in a foreign newspaper
accessible to a public authority under a law
requested only by a government servant
held by any private individual in any circumstances
accepted.x: Information concerning a private body is covered when it is accessible to a public authority under a law.
accepted.tq: Apply the statutory limiting condition instead of treating all private information as automatically accessible.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the ‘right to information’ under Section 2(j)?
o: Compelling an authority to create a new explanation or opinion
Taking notes, extracts or certified copies
Taking certified samples of material
Inspection of works, documents and records
accepted.x: Section 2(j) includes inspection, notes, extracts, certified copies, certified samples and electronic information. It does not require an authority to create a new explanation or opinion.
accepted.tq: Find the option that demands creation of information rather than access to existing information.

accepted.s: A citizen seeks information from a public authority by e-mail in the local official language and claims the BPL fee waiver. Which of the following is correct?
o: The local official language may be used only before a State Information Commission
The request is invalid because only English applications are permitted
The request is valid in principle, and the fee is waived for a BPL applicant
E-mail requests are valid only when made by a public servant
accepted.x: An RTI request may be made by post, in person or by e-mail in Hindi, English or the local official language. The application fee is waived for applicants below the poverty line.
accepted.tq: Combine the rules on mode, language and fee waiver in a practical situation.

accepted.s:
With reference to the nature and constitutional basis of the RTI, consider the following statements:
1. The RTI is a statutory right.
2. It gives effect to the fundamental right to know under Article 19(1)(a).
3. It is available to every person, irrespective of citizenship.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The RTI is a statutory right giving effect to the fundamental right to know under Article 19(1)(a). Under the Act, only citizens can apply, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Separate the constitutional rationale from the statutory eligibility condition.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT among the stated objectives of the RTI Act?
o: Promoting transparency and an informed citizenry
Harmonising disclosure with legitimate confidentiality needs
Replacing the entire system of representative government with direct administration
Containing corruption and holding governments accountable
accepted.x: The Act seeks transparency, accountability, reduced corruption and an informed citizenry while recognising confidentiality needs. It does not seek to replace representative government.
accepted.tq: Identify the option unrelated to the stated purposes of the legislation.

accepted.s: Who is empowered to impose the penalty under Section 20 of the RTI Act?
o: The Central or State Information Commission
The applicant through a private complaint
The concerned Public Information Officer
The District Collector alone
accepted.x: The Central Information Commission or State Information Commission may impose the Section 20 penalty on the concerned Public Information Officer.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the statutory authority imposing the penalty.

accepted.s: The penalty under Section 20 of the RTI Act is imposed at the rate of
o: ₹500 per day, subject to a maximum of ₹50,000
₹100 per day, subject to a maximum of ₹10,000
₹1,000 per day, without any maximum limit
₹250 per day, subject to a maximum of ₹25,000
accepted.x: The penalty is ₹250 per day until the application is received or information is furnished, subject to a maximum of ₹25,000.
accepted.tq: Recall both parts of the penalty formula: daily rate and statutory ceiling.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated ground for imposing a penalty on a Public Information Officer?
o: Disclosing information within the prescribed time
Knowingly giving incorrect or misleading information
Refusing to receive an RTI application
Destroying information or obstructing its disclosure
accepted.x: Penalty grounds include refusal to receive an application, delay, mala fide denial, knowingly incorrect or misleading information, destruction of information and obstruction. Timely disclosure is not a ground for penalty.
accepted.tq: Find the conduct that is compliant rather than penal in nature.

accepted.s: Before imposing a penalty under Section 20, the Public Information Officer
o: must be removed from service immediately
must obtain permission from the applicant
must be given an opportunity of being heard
must prove the applicant's mala fides
accepted.x: The PIO must be heard before penalty is imposed. The burden of proof in the penalty proceeding lies on the PIO.
accepted.tq: Distinguish procedural fairness from the separate rule regarding burden of proof.

accepted.s: In proceedings relating to penalty under Section 20, the burden of proof is placed on the
o: applicant
public authority's minister
Public Information Officer
Central Vigilance Commission
accepted.x: The burden of proof is on the Public Information Officer in the Section 20 penalty proceeding.
accepted.tq: Track the statutory burden rather than assuming that the complainant must prove the entire case.

accepted.s: Apart from imposing a monetary penalty, the Information Commission may also
o: amend the RTI Act by executive order
dissolve the concerned State Government
recommend disciplinary action against the PIO
cancel the applicant's citizenship
accepted.x: The Commission may recommend disciplinary action against the Public Information Officer in addition to imposing the statutory penalty.
accepted.tq: Separate the Commission’s disciplinary recommendation from powers belonging to other authorities.

accepted.s: Under Section 19(8)(b), the Information Commission may require the public authority to
o: provide lifetime employment to the applicant
compensate the applicant for loss suffered
pay a penalty directly to the Information Commissioner
withdraw all exemptions under Section 8
accepted.x: Section 19(8)(b) enables the Commission to require the public authority to compensate the applicant for any loss or other detriment suffered.
accepted.tq: Distinguish compensation for the applicant from the separate penalty imposed on the PIO.

accepted.s:
Which of the following is the most appropriate description of the achievements attributed to the RTI Act?
1. It has helped break the culture of secrecy.
2. It has strengthened citizen participation and service delivery.
3. It has reduced corruption and misuse of public funds.
4. It has completely eliminated corruption in public administration.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: The Act has helped break secrecy, improve accountability, reduce corruption and misuse of public funds, and strengthen participation and service delivery. It has not completely eliminated corruption.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme claim of complete elimination while retaining the qualified achievements.
accepted.sec: Achievements vs misuse - transparency gains, frivolous and vexatious applications

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The RTI Act has generally increased the sense of responsibility in the bureaucracy.
Reason (R): The Act has made access to government information more transparent and has strengthened accountability.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true. Greater transparency and accountability provide the basis for increased responsibility among officials.
accepted.tq: Test whether the reason explains the administrative effect stated in the assertion.
accepted.sec: Achievements vs misuse - transparency gains, frivolous and vexatious applications

accepted.s: Which of the following is an example of misuse of the RTI Act by applicants?
o: Using information to participate in public affairs
Seeking certified copies of government documents
Using RTI for frivolous or vexatious personal disputes and blackmail
Making a request for inspection of public records
accepted.x: Frivolous, vexatious or bulk applications, including use of RTI for personal disputes or blackmail, are identified as forms of applicant misuse.
accepted.tq: Distinguish legitimate access to records from demands made for harassment or private leverage.
accepted.sec: Achievements vs misuse - transparency gains, frivolous and vexatious applications

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Applicants — excessive use of Section 8 to deny information
Public authorities — frivolous personal disputes and blackmail
Applicants — clogging offices with indiscriminate demands
Public authorities — use of RTI for private disputes
accepted.x: C—even offices with indiscriminate demands is attributed to misuse by applicants. Excessive use of Section 8, delays and misleading replies are forms of misuse by public authorities.
accepted.tq: Separate the two columns by identifying who performs the action rather than focusing only on the action itself.
accepted.sec: Achievements vs misuse - transparency gains, frivolous and vexatious applications

accepted.s: Which of the following represents misuse of the RTI Act by public authorities?
o: Making bulk applications for personal disputes
Excessive and bad-faith use of Section 8 exemptions to deny information
Inspecting documents and records
Seeking certified samples of material
accepted.x: Public-authority misuse includes excessive or bad-faith reliance on Section 8 exemptions, along with delayed, incomplete or misleading replies and weak proactive disclosure.
accepted.tq: Use the actor-based distinction between applicant misuse and authority misuse.
accepted.sec: Achievements vs misuse - transparency gains, frivolous and vexatious applications

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The RTI Act has been misused by both members of the public and public authorities.
Reason (R): Applicants may file frivolous or bulk requests, while authorities may delay replies or invoke Section 8 in bad faith.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both the assertion and reason are true. The reason identifies the two distinct forms of misuse by applicants and public authorities.
accepted.tq: Link the general conclusion to concrete examples supplied in the reason.
accepted.sec: Achievements vs misuse - transparency gains, frivolous and vexatious applications

accepted.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 described India's RTI regime as ‘uniquely broad’ and associated it with a possible chilling effect on
o: private investment in agriculture alone
electoral competition only
judicial appointments only
honest decision-making
accepted.x: The Economic Survey associated the uniquely broad RTI regime with a possible chilling effect on honest decision-making and proposed re-examination of the framework.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive quoted description with the precise effect linked to it.
accepted.sec: Achievements vs misuse - transparency gains, frivolous and vexatious applications

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the risks faced by RTI activists and whistle-blowers?
o: They are automatically protected from prosecution under the RTI Act
They may face harassment, legal intimidation and physical attacks
They are prohibited from seeking information about public authorities
They face only civil liability for filing applications
accepted.x: RTI activists and whistle-blowers face harassment, legal intimidation and physical attacks in connection with their disclosures and applications.
accepted.tq: Select the option that captures the complete range of risks rather than a single form of pressure.
accepted.sec: RTI activists' safety - attacks and whistle-blower protection

accepted.s: More than how many RTI activists were reported to have been killed by July 2026?
o: More than 10
More than 25
More than 50
More than 100
accepted.x: Reports cited that more than 100 RTI activists had been killed by July 2026.
accepted.tq: Recall the reported threshold and avoid confusing it with lower estimates.

accepted.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended that the RTI framework should be linked firmly with
o: the law on preventive detention
the law on municipal taxation
the law on parliamentary privileges
the law on whistle-blower protection
accepted.x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended firmly linking RTI with whistle-blower protection to prevent victimisation of those who disclose information.
accepted.tq: Identify the protection mechanism that directly addresses victimisation of information-seekers.
accepted.sec: RTI activists' safety - attacks and whistle-blower protection

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about whistle-blower protection in India:
1. The Whistle Blowers Protection Act was enacted in 2014.
2. The Act has not been operationalised.
3. A 2015 amendment Bill sought to dilute the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 exists, has not been operationalised, and a 2015 amendment Bill sought to dilute it.
accepted.tq: Use the complete sequence of enactment, non-operationalisation and proposed dilution.
accepted.sec: RTI activists' safety - attacks and whistle-blower protection

accepted.s: Which one of the following best explains the recommendation to protect RTI activists through whistle-blower legislation?
o: To exempt activists from all criminal laws
To allow activists to impose penalties on Public Information Officers
To enable activists to appoint Information Commissioners
To prevent victimisation for exposing information in the public interest
accepted.x: The recommendation seeks to prevent victimisation, harassment and attacks against persons who disclose information in the public interest.
accepted.tq: Connect the institutional recommendation with the harm it is intended to prevent.
accepted.sec: RTI activists' safety - attacks and whistle-blower protection
